Alice: quick async check-in — what I did / blockers / today
Alice: did: merged PR #842 (route fallback + canary split 95/5), validated traffic shaping in staging
Alice: blocker: intermittent 429s on /v1/generate during bursts >50 rps, looks like queue depth spike on gpux-03
Alice: today: gonna flip continuous-batching to conservative and monitor; @Ben can you re-run the 1-min burst test when you have a moment?
Ben: saw the same 429s this morning. digging into autoscaler logs now. looks like a short QDepth spike at 09:12
Ben: snippet from staging logs: `2026-03-17T09:12:03Z QDepth=312 inflight=28 gpux-03`
Alice: thanks — here's the load command I used earlier if helpful:
```bash
heyload --concurrency 80 --rps 120 --duration 60 https://staging.api.redwood/v1/generate
```
Carmen: I'll pair on the autoscaler tweak with @Ben after lunch. no blockers on my side. doing authz rollout for JWT rotation (PR #855) today.
Jin: quick code review note on #842 — route precedence test missing for prefix edge-case. pushed small test commit.
Emma: heads-up: sales demo at 15:00 PT, want to avoid regressions. if we see more 429s please flag and fallback to the smaller model variant. :eyes:
Faisal: I'll try reducing max_batch_tokens for the problem model to 1024 and restart the serving instance on gpux-03, then watch for QDepth changes.
deploy-bot: canary deploy started for commit abc123 -> gw-service (staging) :rocket:
Alice: solid. if the QDepth doesn't drop after batch size change, fallback plan is to route burst traffic to model-x-small and enable prefix caching for high-frequency clients. will post follow-up in this thread. :thumbsup:
